title: Classify a Number
description: Read one integer and print Positive if it is greater than zero, Negative if it is less than zero, or Zero if it equals zero.
output_format: Print exactly Positive, Negative, or Zero.

learning_content.title: Conditional statements
learning_content.intro: A condition lets a program choose one path based on whether a comparison is true or false. The branches must cover positive, negative and zero values.
points: Check whether it is greater than zero.
Otherwise check whether it is less than zero.
If neither condition is true, the value is zero.
learning_content.note: Only a fixed number of comparisons are evaluated.

quiz.question: For number = 0, which branch should run in the three-way classification?

options.label: Positive branch
options.feedback: Zero is not greater than zero.

options.label: Negative branch
options.feedback: Zero is not less than zero.

options.label: Else branch
options.feedback: Both greater-than-zero and less-than-zero conditions are false for zero.

options.label: Both comparison branches
options.feedback: An if/else-if chain selects only the first matching branch.

quiz.explanation: Zero is neither greater than nor less than zero, so the final else branch handles it.
